tier1.customer: Breastfeeding or formula-feeding mother, 0-12 weeks postpartum, doing 100% of night care with no partner in the home at all
tier1.scene: There is no partner to negotiate with. Cultural norms assign night care to the mother by default, and there is no agreed system — so every night is renegotiated by exhaustion.
tier1.pain: Nobody owns the night, so the default becomes she owns all of it. Doing 100% of nights, every night, for weeks — with no partner shift to hand off to.
tier1.failed_attempt: There is no agreed system, so every night is renegotiated by exhaustion and resentment. Asking for help from extended family or friends can feel like admitting failure.

emotional_stake.text: She is not just tired — she keeps score alone. Nobody helps you; you are all by yourself. Every uninterrupted hour someone else gets feels like proof her exhaustion is invisible.

insight.text: A roster does not require a partner. It requires a named shift and a named person to cover it — a support web, not a marriage contract. The night still needs an owner and a schedule.
insight.label: Strategic Synthesis

mechanism.text: Schedules a support-web roster — named shifts for family, friends, or paid help — so the mother's protected block is physically real. A sleep banker makes exhaustion visible and tradeable even without a partner.

tier2.desired_change: Nights with zero protected block become a protected block of 3+ hours on most nights. The support web covers named shifts instead of the mother owning every night alone.
tier2.angle: Nobody helps you; you are all by yourself. Cultural norms assign night care to the mother by default, and there is no agreed system. A roster does not require a partner — it requires a named shift and a named person to cover it. Build a support web, not a marriage contract. Give the night a schedule tonight.

tier3.counter_evidence_acknowledged: This is not baby sleep training, and it is not a substitute for medical or mental-health care. When exhaustion is more than tiredness, stop and route out.
